thread:
maya.r: Hi folks, first on-call rotation tomorrow morning. Ran into two setup hiccups: 1) I cant open the infra runbook (403 on Confluence), 2) my ssh jumpbox key isnt letting me into prod proxies. Whos the right contact for each?
casey: welcome! For Confluence perms ping @lina, shes who manages team spaces. For jumpbox, open a ticket in eng-tools or DM me and Ill escalate.
oncall-bot: Heads up: new on-call starters should complete the onboarding checklist: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/oncall/pages/oncall-onboarding-checklist
maya.r: thanks Casey. Lina, can you add me to "Infra Runbooks"? my email is maya.r@redwood.com
lina: added you to the space, you should have view access now. If you still see a 403, try clearing cookies or use incognito.
maya.r: runbook access fixed  thank you! about the jumpbox: when I ssh I get `Permission denied (publickey)`. I uploaded my pubkey to the onboarding form.
casey: eng-tools-bot will show when the key was registered.
eng-tools-bot: Key registration for maya.r: received at 2026-03-21T14:05Z, status: pending manual approval. Approver: casey.
casey: approved your key now, try again.
maya.r: ok ssh works. quick prod question: whats our minimal PD ack/escalation SLA? I dont want to escalate too early.
casey: we aim to ACK PD alerts within 15 minutes. Critical pages (SRE/P0) require immediate ack and incident channel creation. If latency SLO > 2x or >50% error, escalate to SRE.
maya.r: got it. Any short checklist for what to collect before escalating?
lina: Short checklist: 1) PD incident id and alert summary; 2) `rdw-metrics query --since 5m "latency p95"` screenshot/clip; 3) last 2k lines from relevant service: `rdw-logs get proxy --since 10m | tail -n 2000 > /tmp/incident-$INC.log`; 4) config diff if recent deploy `git log -n 5 --pretty=oneline ops/deploys`
maya.r: thanks, appreciate concrete commands. Is there a shadow shift I can join later today?
oncall-bot: Shadow slots posted on calendar: today 16:00 and 17:00 UTC. Book via the oncall calendar.
casey: I can take the 17:00 slot and walk through an example incident playbook. Bring laptop.
maya.r: perfect, Ill join 17:00. Another Q: after an incident do we always write a postmortem?
lina: postmortem for anything P1/P0 or outage longer than 30m. Use the standard template in ops repo and link runbook sections and owner. Short and actionable.
maya.r: great. Also saw mention of fallback model routing in the runbook  if I ever need to flip traffic, whats the exact command?
casey: we normally avoid manual flips but TL;DR: `rctl traffic set --service model-proxy --policy fallback-v1 && rctl traffic check model-proxy` then notify #incidents. Confirm with SRE if >10% traffic.
maya.r: understood. Thanks all, feel much better. See you at 17:00 for shadow.
lina: welcome to the rotation! :party_parrot:
